decisions.reason: It directly builds on the already accepted BASIC 518 platform, so the firm can exploit strong prior screening knowledge and positive early market recognition to improve and sell it further.

A mobile high-speed flail shredder is close to the firm’s established mobile waste-processing machinery business, giving it the knowledge base and customer access needed to learn from early use and refine the product.

The mobile high-speed grinder fits the firm’s core processing portfolio and customer base, and in capital equipment a one-year market presence is typically too short to abandon such a related product before learning effects emerge.

A stationary electric fine shredder matches the firm’s existing shredding and plant expertise as well as demand for efficient resource-saving recycling solutions, making it a product the firm is well placed to develop further.

This green-waste-focused mobile grinder is a specialized extension of capabilities the firm already has in grinders and biomass/composting applications, so absorptive capacity for improvement and commercialization is high.

Stationary single-shaft pre-shredders are strongly related to the firm’s established stationary recycling machinery and were given a dedicated market presentation, supporting continued commitment and iterative development.
